transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm seeking help because I've been struggling with severe mental health issues for about a year and nine months now. It's been a really difficult time with intense mood shifts and some very unusual experiences. My thoughts feel very jumbled up and hard to follow lately.
Have you ever had times of hallucinations or delusions when you were not also having a manic or depressive mood episode?

Yes, I've definitely had times like that. There were periods lasting at least two or three weeks where I was hearing voices and having very strong, unusual beliefs, even though my mood felt completely normal and stable. I wasn't feeling that manic high or extra energy at all during those weeks.

Have there also been times when you had a full manic episode or a major depressive episode that lasted for most of the illness, or have the psychotic symptoms been present on their own for long stretches?

Yes, those high-energy manic phases have actually been present for the majority of the time I've been unwell over the past year and nine months. However, there were still those clear periods of at least two weeks where the voices and delusions continued even after my mood and energy went back to normal.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type), Schizophrenia], but the interview now shows a clear history of psychosis occurring for at least 2–3 weeks when mood was normal, while manic symptoms were present for the majority of the illness. That pattern supports schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type, and makes schizophrenia less likely because mood episodes have been prominent for much of the course rather than psychosis occurring only outside mood episodes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a prolonged illness with recurrent manic episodes for the majority of the course, plus clear periods of at least 2 weeks of hallucinations and delusions occurring when mood was otherwise normal. This satisfies the key feature of schizoaffective disorder: psychosis persisting outside mood episodes, with prominent bipolar/manic symptoms. Bipolar I with psychotic features is less likely because psychosis also occurs during euthymic periods; schizophrenia is less likely because manic episodes are present for much of the illness.
